info.name: Program Capacity & Invoice Reservation
info.description:
Program capacity & invoice reservation — a backend-only service that tracks a
financing programme's credit limit in real time.

**Run it in three commands**

1. `docker compose up -d && npm ci && npm run prisma:generate`
2. `npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma db seed`
3. `npm run start:dev`  (http://localhost:3000, Swagger at /docs)

The seed creates everything this collection needs — two programmes, four
currencies, FX rates and an admin user. No manual SQL.

**Then just press Run.** The collection is ordered so it can be executed
top-to-bottom by the Collection Runner: `Login` captures the tokens and mints a
fresh `runId`, so every invoice reference is unique per run and the whole
collection is safe to re-run against the same database as often as you like.
Every request asserts its own status and payload, so a red result is a real
failure rather than something to interpret.

**Seeded login:** `admin@itentio.dev` / `dev-only-password-change-me` (ADMIN).

**Seeded programmes:** `PRG-1` (GBP, 10,000,000 limit) and `PRG-2` (JPY,
1,500,000,000) — the second one exists so the cross-currency path can be driven
without adding data by hand.

**Worth knowing while testing:** `POST /auth/login` is rate limited to 5
requests/minute and everything else to 100/minute. Each full run of this
collection spends two of those five, so running it three times inside one minute
will be throttled — that is the service behaving correctly, and `Login` says so
explicitly rather than letting it surface as a cascade of 401s. Wait a minute
and run again. Access tokens last 1h; `Refresh token` rotates the pair and
invalidates the old refresh token immediately.

exec: // requestedAt is business metadata and must not be in the future, so it is
// a timestamp a minute in the past. It is set ONCE per run (by Login) and
// only seeded here as a fallback: regenerating it per request would change
// the body between a reservation and its replay, and an Idempotency-Key
// replayed with a different body is a 409, not a replay.

item.name: 0 · Setup (read me)
item.description:
Nothing to do here — `npx prisma db seed` already created it all. This folder
just says what you are working with.

**Programmes**
- `PRG-1` — GBP, limit 10,000,000. The `programRef` variable points here.
- `PRG-2` — JPY, limit 1,500,000,000. Used by the cross-currency folder: a GBP
  invoice reserved against it comes back converted and rounded to whole yen.

**Currencies and FX:** GBP, USD, EUR, JPY, with rates into GBP.

**User:** `admin@itentio.dev` / `dev-only-password-change-me`, role ADMIN.

There is deliberately no endpoint that *creates* a programme — that is treated
as back-office data entry rather than part of the reserve/release/query surface
(docs/DECISIONS.md ADR-13). To add your own, use `npx prisma studio`.

**Roles.** `reserve` and `release` require ADMIN or OPERATOR; availability is
open to any authenticated role; discrepancies are ADMIN-only. The seeded user is
ADMIN, so every request here succeeds. To see a 403, create a READER user in
Prisma Studio and log in as them.

item.name: Refresh token — replay the spent one

request.description: Replaying a rotated-away refresh token is treated as evidence of a leak: it is rejected, and every unrevoked token in that user's family is revoked as well.
Every business endpoint sits behind a global JWT guard. Only /health, /auth/login and /auth/refresh are public.
Current limit, reserved amount and remaining availability. All money is a fixed-scale string at the programme currency's minor units, never a JSON number.
Reserves part of the programme's limit for an invoice. The Idempotency-Key is fixed for this run so the next request can replay it.

item.name: Reserve a GBP invoice against the JPY programme

request.description: The invoice is in GBP, the programme in JPY. The rate is resolved at reservation time (here by inverting the seeded JPY→GBP rate), applied once, and the result is quantised to JPY's zero decimal places — so the booked amount is whole yen. The rate is then frozen on the invoice.

request.description: Releases the frozen programme-currency amount, so the JPY programme returns to precisely its prior availability rather than to today's rate.

item.name: Reject a JPY amount carrying decimals

request.description: JPY has no minor unit, so `1000.5` is malformed input rather than a rounding opportunity. It is refused instead of being booked as a different number.

request.description: The capacity test lives in the WHERE clause of the debiting UPDATE, so there is no read-modify-write window: the programme can never be over-committed, no matter how many callers race.

item.name: Reserve an invoice (setup for the next request)

request.description: Books INV-…-DUP at 100.00 so the next request can try to change its terms behind the same reference.

A fresh Idempotency-Key, but the same invoice reference carrying a different amount. Confirming the earlier reservation here would answer 201 with the ORIGINAL figure to a caller who asked for a different one, so it is a conflict instead.
Tidies up so the run leaves no capacity held.

item.name: Idempotency-Key reused with a different body

request.description: That key was already settled against a different body earlier in this run. The fingerprint covers the method, the concrete URL and the body, so this is a conflict rather than a replay.
The header is mandatory on both mutating endpoints.

No sign is accepted. A negative amount would satisfy the guarded UPDATE's predicate and *lower* the reserved amount, so it is rejected at the edge rather than by a CHECK constraint three statements later.
A reservation of nothing is not a valid instruction.

item.name: Amount too precise for the currency

request.description: GBP has two decimal places; a third is malformed input, not something to round away silently.
Currencies are a table, not a free-text field.

Every query is parameterised, so this was never going to execute — but it is still refused by validation rather than being stored. Run `Get availability` afterwards to confirm the service is unharmed.
An unknown programme reference is a 404, not a 500.
Nothing to release.

Where reconciliation puts anything it could not make agree with the treasury snapshot — an unknown invoice, an amount drift, a currency mismatch, or a programme left over its limit. Normally empty until a snapshot has been consumed from Kafka. ADMIN only: this is operator information, not client information.
Liveness probe, deliberately unauthenticated because it exposes no business data. It is liveness only — it does not check Postgres or the Kafka consumer (ADR-13).
